Name: near_duplicate_needle_crossover
Title: Bigger Banks Help Retrieval Only Through Near-Duplicates the Reader Cannot Find in Context: Bank Size x Near-Duplicate Rate on WebShop and ALFWorld
Short Hypothesis: The growth of top-k retrieval's advantage over the whole-bank-in-context route with bank size is a near-duplicate effect. On WebShop (one procedure, instance-specific product and option bindings), with near-duplicates replaced by same-category trajectories that share no bindings, retrieval, the whole bank and the best static prompt are within the noise floor at every bank size; with near-duplicates planted, retrieval's gain is carried by the needle's instance bindings (a needle with its product identifiers and option values redacted but its query and procedure intact gives less than a third of it), requires the needle to be retrieved and is used once retrieved even without its instruction line, and the whole-bank route recovers less than half of it, the recovered fraction falling as the haystack grows from 12 to 40 items with the distractor composition held fixed. On ALFWorld the measured +17.2 net residual of retrieval over the best static arm is carried by near-duplicates at the binding level the goal sentence exposes (task type, object, receptacle): removing them, measured against a fixed type-conditioned static arm whose exemplars sit inside the same bank, removes at least half of the residual, a partial match (object or receptacle) carries part of it, and the same-scene manipulation (bindings the goal sentence does not expose) leaves retrieval unmoved.
Related Work: Synapse (arxiv:2306.07863) introduced trajectory-as-exemplar prompting with state abstraction and an exemplar memory retrieved by similarity on MiniWoB++ and Mind2Web, without a whole-bank or random-selection control; ExpeL and Agent Workflow Memory likewise assume retrieval over experience on WebShop-style tasks. arxiv:2603.18272 trains agents to use retrieved trajectories without a fixed or random exemplar control. Bertsch et al. (arxiv:2405.00200) find that long-context ICL gains come from attention to similar examples so that random many-shot converges to retrieval on classification, and arxiv:2412.16926 that selection matters less with long context; arxiv:2411.05000 shows in-context lookup degrading with context on synthetic threads. arxiv:2607.26497 sweeps corpus size on documents with one reader and scores recall. The archived order_randomized_leakage_audit observed near-duplicate leakage in task streams, and decorative_retriever observed that retrieval-set overlap predicts retrieval necessity; neither planted or removed near-duplicates or ran a whole-bank arm. The home Measurement C (runs/STEP0_RESULTS.md) measured k3 minus the best static arm (static3, three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars) at +17.2 net on ALFWorld's natural bank, with unseen (+20.1) above seen (+14.3); it observed the natural pool and did not manipulate it.
Abstract: Bank-size sweeps in retrieval are done on document corpora with one reader and scored on recall; for agent experience banks the operative question is why a larger bank helps retrieval at all, and whether the whole bank in context would do the same. We hypothesise that the bank-size curve of top-k retrieval on trajectory banks is a near-duplicate coverage curve, and that the whole-bank route's curve is an in-context lookup curve that falls as the haystack grows. On WebShop (one procedure, instance-specific product and option bindings) we build per-cluster banks of state-abstracted successful trajectories at 12 and 40 items that hold a near-duplicate (same product, or same category with two shared attribute phrases) for every test instruction or for none, the remaining slots filled by same-category trajectories that share no attribute phrase with any cluster instruction, with the filler set held fixed across sizes. Three further banks decouple what the near-duplicate is from whether it is found: a redacted needle (product identifiers and option values masked, query and procedure intact), a hidden needle (instruction line templated, body intact, retrievability measured by a retriever that indexes line and body), and hard-negative fillers that share attribute phrases with the test instructions. Banks are read by top-2 retrieval, whole in a cached prefix, or through fixed-exemplar and compiled-procedure static prompts. On ALFWorld the manipulation is applied at the binding level the goal sentence exposes (none, partial, full match on task type, object, receptacle), against a fixed type-conditioned static arm whose exemplars sit inside every bank, and on seen scenes at the scene level, and is stated against the measured +17.2 net residual of retrieval over the best static arm. We predict no retrieval residual over the best static arm or the whole bank without near-duplicates, a gain that needs the needle's bindings and needs the needle to be retrieved, a whole-bank recovery below half that shrinks from 12 to 40 items, and on ALFWorld a residual at least halved by removing binding-level near-duplicates while the scene-level manipulation leaves retrieval unmoved. Task success is primary, needle hit and needle-use rates are mediators, and cost is measured under prefix caching.
Experiments:
- WebShop (public data; a day of install). Reader Qwen3-32B, one vLLM replica per GPU, prefix caching. Standard 500 test instructions; 4 seeds for confirmatory cells (2,000 paired episodes), 2 for secondary; identical seeds and order across arms. k=0 runs first; its seeds 1-2 vs 3-4 difference is the paired floor (about +/-3 points at 2,000 episodes, +/-4.5 at 1,000).
- Bank: Qwen3-32B successes on 2,000+ train instructions (600-800 items) plus public human demonstrations; Synapse-style state abstraction (top-5 result lines; product title, price, options, buy) on both routes; items truncated to 300 tokens (40 items about 12k).
- Needles: a trajectory for the test product id (constructed: paraphrased instruction, attribute subset, different price cap, run to success within 3 attempts) or same category with two shared attribute phrases; reported separately. Instructions without a needle are dropped from every cell (450+ expected).
- Clusters of 5 retained instructions from one category with disjoint attribute phrases (about 90); each needle matches one cluster instruction. Fillers sib-0: same-category train trajectories sharing no attribute phrase with any cluster instruction; one 35-item set per cluster, the 7-item size-12 set a subset. Size 40: r=1 = 5 needles + 35 sib-0, r=0 = 40 sib-0; size 12: 5 + 7, and 12 sib-0. r=1x (redacted): r=1 with every product identifier in the needle body (result ids and titles, clicked id, product title, option values) replaced by placeholders; query, actions and instruction line intact. r=1h (hidden): r=1 with each needle's instruction line replaced by the category template, body intact. r=1hn: 5 needles + sib-1 hard negatives (same category, at least one attribute phrase shared with a cluster instruction, different product): 35 at size 40, a 7-subset at size 12.
- Retriever: BM25 plus embedding over instruction line plus abstracted body, top-2, uncached; needle hit rate logged. Whole-bank: the cluster bank as a cached prefix warmed once per cluster per seed. Static arms: Baselines.
- WebShop counts. 4 seeds (2,000 each): k=0, fixed-2, RET-40 r=0/r=1/r=1x/r=1h, WB-40 r=0/r=1, WB-12 r=0/r=1 (10 arms, 20,000). 2 seeds (1,000 each): compiled (to 4 seeds if it beats fixed-2), WB-40 r=1h, RET-12 r=1hn, RET-40 r=1hn (4,000-5,000). Exploratory (G16): Qwen3-8B on k=0, RET-40 r=0/r=1, WB-40 r=0/r=1 at 1 seed (2,500; dropped first if throughput is below 800/h). About 27,000 episodes at about 1,000/h on two GPUs: 27 h, plus 3 h of bank construction.
- ALFWorld (installed; Measurement C reader and serving). Items: train expert trajectories, about 140 tokens. Binding levels for a test game: full = same (type, object class, receptacle class); partial = same type and one of the two; none = same type, neither. Per-game banks of 72 (12 per type, type-agnostic); the 12 same-type items always include static3-none's three exemplars (Baselines); r=0 = 12 none-level; r=partial = one partial match (object or receptacle, alternating by game) + 11 none; r=1 = one different-scene full match + 11 none. Scene cells (valid_seen games with a same-scene full-match train item, at least 90): scene-r1 uses it, scene-r0 a different-scene full match. Routes: RET k=3 by goal text (as k3 in Measurement C); WB-72 as a cached per-game prefix (about 10k tokens).
- ALFWorld counts. 274 games x 4 seeds (1,096 each): RET-72 r=0/partial/r=1, WB-72 r=0/r=1, static3-none; static3 on seeds 3-4 (548): 7,124. Scene: 2 arms x (at least 90 games x 4-6 seeds), about 1,200. Exploratory 274 x 2: WB-24 r=1 (haystack replicate of P3b), 548. About 8,900 at 730/h: 12 h.
- Outcomes: success primary (WebShop reward = 1); WebShop mean reward secondary; mediators and cost per Measurement.
- Order: install; k=0 and floor; bank and needles; P1a gate (15 points or stop); pre-registration; confirmatory cells with ALFWorld on the second replica; secondary cells; 8B. About 39 h on two A100s after install.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Static arms as the baseline on WebShop: fixed-2 (two fixed sib-0 items from one category, identical for all clusters, cached), compiled (one procedure paragraph: search, pick, options, buy; cached), k=0; best static = the highest at matched tokens, and every retrieval and whole-bank number is the arm minus it on the same (instruction, seed). On ALFWorld: static3 (Measurement C's three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, +12.4 over k0, re-run on seeds 3-4) anchors the +17.2; static3-none is the matched-pool static arm: three fixed expert exemplars per type whose object and receptacle classes appear in no evaluation goal (chosen once from train; if a type has none, the least-colliding exemplars are used and colliding games are logged and excluded from the r=0 contrast), about 430 tokens, cached, type-conditioned, and present in every bank so that retrieval and the whole bank select from a pool containing the static arm's items; instr_all from Measurement C is the type-agnostic reference and WB-72 is type-agnostic by construction.
- Whole-bank at two haystack sizes (12 and 40 on WebShop; 72 confirmatory and 24 exploratory on ALFWorld) is the matched-budget no-retriever arm, with filler composition identical across sizes; the r=0 banks are the fixed-selection control at the whole-context budget.
- Near-duplicate rate 0/1 on both routes at size 40; same-product versus shared-attribute needles and shared-attribute count as graded near-duplicate strength.
- Redacted needle (product identifiers and option values masked, query and procedure intact): what in the near-duplicate carries the gain.
- Hidden needle (instruction line templated, body intact) under a retriever that indexes line and body: retrievability measured, not constructed; the needle-hit subset against r=1 on the same instructions; the whole-bank route with and without the line.
- Hard-negative fillers (sib-1) at 12 versus 40 on retrieval: whether the retriever's size curve is a hit-rate curve; sib-0 fillers kept for the whole-bank size cells so only the count varies there.
- ALFWorld binding ladder none/partial/full at 4 seeds against the static arm drawn from the same bank; the scene manipulation with the full match held fixed; static3 minus static3-none as the observational read of incidental partial matches inside Measurement C's fixed exemplars.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (gate; what the needle carries; 4 seeds, floor +/-3). (a) RET-40 r=1 minus RET-40 r=0 is at least 15 points; within the floor: the sibling transfers as well as the needle and the design stops; between: no claim. (b) RET-40 r=1x (product identifiers masked, query and procedure intact) minus RET-40 r=0 is below one third of the gain: the near-duplicate's value is its bindings. Falsified if r=1x retains at least half of the gain: the value is instance-specific query wording the reader re-issues, not the bindings.
- P2 (no residual without near-duplicates): at r=0, |RET-40 minus best static (fixed-2, compiled, k=0)| and |RET-40 minus WB-40 r=0| are within the floor. Falsified if either exceeds one third of the gain (5 points) in either direction: siblings carry category wording that no static arm supplies, or they distract. Between: undecided.
- P3 (headline: the reader cannot find the needle and finds it less as the haystack grows; fillers identical at both sizes): (a) WB-40's recovery, (WB-40 r=1 minus r=0)/(RET-40 r=1 minus r=0), has a paired-bootstrap upper bound below 0.5; (b) WB-12 r=1 exceeds WB-40 r=1 by at least one third of the gain (five needles among 7 vs 35 fillers); (c) needle-use (first query equals the needle's) is at least 20 points lower in WB-40 r=1 than in RET-40 r=1, WB-12 r=1 at least 10 above WB-40 r=1. Falsified if the recovery's lower bound exceeds 0.5, or WB-40 r=1's needle-use is within the floor of RET-40 r=1's (the reader locates the needle: arxiv:2405.00200 on trajectories), or WB-12 minus WB-40 is within the floor. Recoveries of 0.25-0.5 are undecided (Measurement).
- P4 (a retrieved needle is used without its instruction line; the whole-bank lookup does not need it; retrievability measured): the retriever indexes line plus body, so the templated needle's top-2 hit rate h in r=1h is logged (expected 0.3-0.7). (a) On the instructions where the needle is retrieved, RET-40 r=1h minus r=0 is at least two thirds of the same instructions' RET-40 r=1 minus r=0 (4 seeds). Falsified if at most one third: the reader recognises the exemplar by its instruction line, so presence in the retrieved set is not use. Undecided if h is below 0.15. (b) WB-40 r=1h is within the floor (+/-4.5, 2 seeds) of WB-40 r=1; falsified if at least half of the gain below: the whole-bank route's partial recovery is a lexical match on the instruction line.
- P5 (ALFWorld, against Measurement C's +17.2 net residual of k3 over static3; 274 x 4, floor about +/-5.7 net). (a) Binding ladder: RET-72 r=0 minus static3-none is below +8.6 net (selection among same-type items sharing no goal binding, from a pool holding the static arm's items, is worth less than half of the residual); RET-72 r=partial minus r=0 is at least one third of r=1 minus r=0; RET-72 r=1 minus static3 must exceed +8.6 (calibration). Falsified if RET-72 r=0 minus static3-none is at least +12 net: selection among binding-mismatched items (by shared object-origin receptacle or scene, the logged mediators) carries the residual and the goal-binding account fails on ALFWorld; or if r=partial minus r=0 is within the floor while r=1 minus r=0 exceeds +8.6: only the exact pair counts. (b) Scene: on valid_seen games with a same-scene full match (seeds added until the paired floor is at most +/-8 net), scene-r1 minus scene-r0 is below +8 net; falsified at +12 or more. (c) Exploratory: WB-72 r=1's recovery with its interval; WB-24 vs WB-72 r=1 (haystack replicate of P3b).
- P6 (retrieval's size curve is a coverage curve, not a hit-rate curve, under fillers that can displace the needle): with sib-1 hard negatives the logged needle hit rate stays above 0.8 at 12 and 40 and RET-40 r=1hn is within the floor (+/-4.5, 2 seeds) of RET-12 r=1hn. Falsified if the hit rate at 40 falls below 0.6 and RET-40 r=1hn is at least half of the gain below RET-12 r=1hn: the retriever loses the needle as the haystack grows and the size effect is reported per logged hit rate.
Measurement and Noise Control: WebShop: paired per (instruction, seed) with identical seeds and instruction order across arms; confirmatory cells at 500 x 4 (floor about +/-3 points of success, measured before pre-registration as the k=0 seeds 1-2 versus 3-4 difference on the retained paired set), secondary cells at 500 x 2 (about +/-4.5); recovery fractions, needle-use rates and the P4 needle-hit subset carry paired-bootstrap intervals over instructions. Margins are fractions of the P1a gain (RET-40 r=1 minus RET-40 r=0, gate at least 15 points): on 4-seed cells effects must exceed the floor and one third of the gain (5 points at the gate), on 2-seed cells half of it (7.5); an effect between the floor and its margin is undecided. P3's rule (bootstrap upper bound of the recovery fraction below 0.5) has power at true recoveries up to about 0.25 with a 15-point gain and a +/-3 floor; the decidable range is pre-registered from the measured gain. P4a is computed on the instructions where the templated needle was retrieved (about 1,000 episodes at h=0.5, floor about +/-4.5), paired against the same instructions' r=1 and r=0 outcomes; its floor is re-measured on that subset and (a) is undecided if the subset is below 300 episodes. ALFWorld: 274 games x 4 seeds paired on (game, seed), with static3 re-run on the added seeds and static3-none run on all four; floor about +/-5.7 net (the brief's +/-8 at 274 x 2 scaled by 1/sqrt(2)); margins against Measurement C's +17.2 (half is 8.6 net; falsifier +12 net, above the floor); the partial rung's margin is one third of the measured r=1 minus r=0 difference; the scene subset adds seeds (4-6) until its paired floor is at most +/-8 net, falsifier at +12. Mediators per episode: needle hit (needle in the retrieved set), needle-use (first search query equals the needle's; chosen product id logged as a second read; on ALFWorld the first navigation target equals the needle's object location), and on ALFWorld whether retrieved items share the test object's origin receptacle (from expert solutions) or the scene; per-episode binaries with floors near +/-3 at 2,000 episodes, secondary to success. Cost under prefix caching: prefill tokens, cache hit ratio per cluster or game, GPU-seconds per episode. Pre-registration after the floor and the P1a gate.

Risk Factors and Limitations:
- WebShop is not installed on this node (a day of setup) and Qwen3-32B's base success may be low (about 30-40%); the floor is measured at 4 seeds before any claim, and the P1a gate (at least 15 points) is the stop rule: if the near-duplicate leverage is smaller, the downstream margins do not clear the floor and the study stops.
- Same-product needles are constructed by running paraphrased instructions to success; instructions without a constructible needle are dropped from all cells, shrinking the paired set (floor re-measured) and possibly biasing it toward easier products; needle types are reported separately.
- The redacted needle keeps the query, so the reader may re-issue it and pick the product from live results: that is P1b's falsification path, not a leak; the masking is checked by string search for every product identifier before the cell runs.
- The body-indexed retriever may find the hidden needle at a high rate (then the miss subset is small, which P4a does not need) or at a very low one (below 0.15: P4a undecided, reported with the logged rate); the hit subset is a selected set of instructions and is always compared with itself across arms.
- P3's decision rule has power only for true whole-bank recoveries up to about 0.25 at the gate; 0.25-0.5 returns undecided; needle-use is the sharper mechanism read and is reported alongside.
- Per-cluster and per-game banks make the whole-bank prefix cluster- or game-specific; it remains a static, type-agnostic, cached prefix, warmed once per cluster or game with its hit ratio reported.
- State abstraction and the 300-token truncation are required to fit 40 items in 16k and are applied to both routes; results are conditional on that abstraction.
- Self-generated bank items may carry leaked behaviour from near-duplicate train instructions; the human-demonstration subset is analysed separately.
- static3-none requires, per task type, three train exemplars whose object and receptacle classes appear in no evaluation goal; if a type lacks them the least-colliding exemplars are used and colliding games are excluded from the r=0 contrast, which raises its floor (re-measured; seeds added on that subset if above +/-7).
- The ALFWorld claim depends on static3 re-run on the added seeds reproducing Measurement C's +12.4 over k0 within its interval; if the constructed r=1 bank does not reproduce a residual above +8.6, P5a is not interpretable and is reported as such.
- If P5a is falsified, ALFWorld's retrieval residual is selection among non-duplicates and the near-duplicate account is confined to WebShop; if P3 is falsified, the result still bounds when the whole bank substitutes for retrieval; both are reported.
- Only two environment structures are sampled; the cross-environment claim rests on the same manipulation at the binding level each retrieval key exposes.
Addresses gap: G17 (primary): retrieval against a matched-budget whole-bank arm and against fixed selection, here with the near-duplicate rate, content and retrievability manipulated rather than observed, and with the manipulation that should remove the measured ALFWorld residual named and run against a static arm drawn from the same bank; also G20 (trajectory banks on two agent environments rather than document corpora) and G16 (exploratory second reader on the in-context lookup).
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullets: Measurement A ('unseen ~ seen, so the retrieved value is the type's procedure, not the scene') and Measurement C (k3 minus static3 = +17.2 net on the natural bank) observe ALFWorld's natural pool; this idea plants and removes near-duplicates at set binding levels on two environments, names the manipulation that should remove the +17.2 and the static arm it must be measured against, and claims the retrieval-over-whole-bank residual is zero without near-duplicates and grows with them only where the bindings sit in the retrieval key, which neither measurement can say. Nearest digest card: arxiv:2607.26497 measures a corpus-size crossover on documents with one reader scored on recall; this idea claims the bank-size curve of retrieval on trajectory banks is a near-duplicate-coverage curve and the whole-bank route's curve is an in-context lookup curve that falls with haystack size, scored on task success, and tests it with redacted, hidden and hard-negative banks that no recall-scored sweep can run. Nearest archived ideas: order_randomized_leakage_audit (5.7) audited leakage through task order in streams (observed) with no whole-bank comparator; decorative_retriever (5.75) observed retrieval-set overlap; here overlap is built in at two rates, two content levels and two retrievability levels, and the whole-bank route is the alternative under test.
